recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If fixed[x] complex datatype validation regresses, fix the validator code or dependency artifacts rather than this HL7/fhir specification source checkout.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction asking the Java validator to enforce fixed[x] constraints on complex datatypes such as Coding and SimpleQuantity, using the historical Cholesterol profile as the motivating example.
initial_application: The Jira comment records the integrated hapifhir/org.hl7.fhir.core pull request. PR #20 merged on 2019-04-26 with bce35251f3a929da5e645d661e176fc410fad11d modifying InstanceValidator.java for complex fixed values and c3bc29f06aba5def59ec21e9ab19acce7b81eaad adding validator examples. No HL7/fhir source commit mentioning FHIR-21004 or GF#21004 was found.
additional_context: FHIR-I WGM 202001 minutes state that FHIR-21004 was changed to a technical correction because it had already been fixed. The current HL7/fhir checkout consumes org.hl7.fhir.core/org.hl7.fhir.validation as external ca.uhn.hapi.fhir artifacts and contains no InstanceValidator.java. Current source checks found Observation is active, but the only cholesterol-named source file is an example Observation, and fixedCoding/fixedQuantity only appear in QUICK model metadata rather than an active cholesterol profile source.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. The implemented behavior belongs to the external validator repository/artifact stream, and there is no authoritative HL7/fhir source hunk to edit for the requested validator behavior.
